## Themes

These rows serve how an agent acts on a request (stopping on evidence against it, running its own checks), reproducing a bug from the reported actions and driving a real app to prove it, finding the duplicates and regressions among incoming work, helping a person use this harness and word requests, and a guided setup that writes the model roster. The rest serve flows we do not run (chat-driven bug intake, pull-request driving), a working-style skill whose shape is still open, and model choice, which the owner's roster holds. The recommendations are ruled as one set, with named exceptions.

80. skip-deliberate-temporary-duplication: Deliberate temporary duplication while an old path is replaced may be skipped, unless it touches security, billing, data access, API behaviour, or a shared abstraction would clearly cut risk. (references/bugbot-triage.md:47-52)
81. skip-when-enforced-invariant-covers: A warning already guaranteed by a visible shared component, framework contract or type invariant may be skipped, but not when the invariant is assumed, timing-dependent or crosses async or state boundaries. (references/bugbot-triage.md:54-59)
82. skip-owner-declared-follow-up: An issue the PR owner explicitly defers may be skipped when the PR does not worsen it and it is low risk, but not when the agent lacks owner input or it would merge a regression. (references/bugbot-triage.md:61-66)
83. skip-self-withdrawn-finding: A finding the bot itself withdrew or marked compliant may be skipped once verified locally, but not on a bare human "false positive" for a high-risk issue. (references/bugbot-triage.md:68-73)
84. never-auto-skip-categories: Security, privacy, auth, billing, retention, training-data, permission, high-severity, migration, schema, idempotency, concurrency and cross-system findings, plus small clearly risk-reducing fixes, are never auto-skipped. (references/bugbot-triage.md:75-82)
85. past-human-dismissals-are-not-rules: Past human dismissals of security or data-flow comments are treated as owner judgment, not team-wide skip rules. (references/bugbot-triage.md:84)

90. keep-narrow-error-condition: A request to widen a deliberately narrow error condition into a catch-all is declined when the narrowness separates distinct failures, unless the gap is in the same category, loses data, or the retry is idempotent and still surfaces the original error. 104. plan-live-verify-ten-lanes-on-named-model: Live verification must declare ten lanes on a named worker model at the PR head and list lanes numbered exactly 1 to 10. (scripts/check-plan.mjs:7, 156-161)

111. watcher-three-modes: The watcher follows one PR, the connected open stack, or a frozen queued stack until every PR merges, and stack and queued modes are mutually exclusive. (wp/cli.ts:86-109, 140)
112. frozen-queue-list: A queued stack can be given as an explicit bottom-to-top PR list, allowed only in queued mode, non-empty and duplicate-free, with `#` prefixes accepted. (wp/cli.ts:52-66, 105-109, 134-135)
113. watcher-polling-defaults: Defaults are a 60 s poll interval, a 300 s whole-stack sweep, no deadline (0 disables it), and a budget of 5 consecutive query errors, all validated as positive or non-negative numbers. (wp/cli.ts:34-51, 110-128)
114. status-only-snapshot: A status-only flag prints one status table and exits 0, and in queued mode it skips the queue state machine. (wp/cli.ts:129, 211-220)
115. allow-draft-flag: An opt-in flag stops a draft PR from counting as a merge gate. (wp/cli.ts:130; wp/policy.ts:160-170)
116. json-default-pretty-optional: Output is JSON by default (one line per event while polling), with an optional human-readable rendering. (wp/cli.ts:87-89, 131, 184; wp/render.ts:2-3)
117. usage-error-exit-64-stderr-only: Bad arguments exit 64 with the error on stderr and nothing on stdout, and help exits 0 without touching GitHub. (wp/cli.ts:173-183; wp/cli.test.ts:86-104, 156-165, 217)
118. context-resolution-order: Repository and PR come from explicit flags first, then the local `origin` remote, then the current branch's PR via `gh`. (wp/github.ts:648-671, 459-473)
119. canonical-github-url-only: Remote and PR URLs are accepted only as canonical `https://github.com/owner/repo` shapes with no port, credentials, query or fragment, and a bad PR URL is a non-retryable failure. (wp/github.ts:164-221)
120. stack-discovery-bottom-to-top: The stack is rebuilt from open PRs' head and base branches, walking down to the root and up through children in PR-number order, and fork heads are never treated as parents or as having upstream children. (wp/github.ts:672-726)
121. merged-or-closed-short-circuit: A merged or closed PR is classified before any thread or check query. (wp/policy.ts:65-69)
122. checks-fast-path-then-paginated-fallback: Checks are read from `gh pr checks` first, then from a paginated GraphQL rollup when that is empty or unusable, and the read fails as retryable when both are empty. (wp/github.ts:523-544, 613-634)
123. check-states-fail-closed: Unknown or unexpected check states are counted as failed, while incomplete runs and pending or expected statuses count as pending. (wp/github.ts:235-249, 272-306)
124. owner-approval-gate-not-waited-on: A check named as the code-review approval gate is classified as its own kind, never as pending or failed, so the watcher does not wait on a human approval. (wp/github.ts:250-271)
125. full-thread-pagination-drop-resolved: Review threads are paginated to the end, and resolved ones are dropped. (wp/github.ts:356-385, 398-405, 635-647)
126. review-bot-thread-tagging: Threads whose first comment comes from a review bot are tagged, and the number of distinct bot review passes is counted from run-id markers across all pages. (wp/github.ts:329-355, 386-405)
127. strict-response-parsing: Missing keys and unknown enum values in GitHub responses raise retryable errors that carry the raw value, and only the empty review decision is normalised to "none". (wp/github.ts:81-131, 155-163, 407-438)
128. github-refusal-overrides-clean-checks: A blocked merge state with a failing or errored head-commit rollup is treated as failing CI even when every visible check is clean. (wp/policy.ts:8-32, 99-124; wp/types.compile.ts:63-73)
129. previous-passing-ci-flag: Each CI state records whether any earlier commit on the PR had passed. (wp/policy.ts:43-46; wp/render.ts:6)
130. skip-rollup-query-while-queued-pending: In queued mode a PR whose checks are only pending skips the commit-rollup query. (wp/policy.ts:83-91)
131. review-automation-running-flag: A pending check whose name mentions a review bot or security review marks review automation as still running. (wp/policy.ts:53-58, 132-138)
132. blocker-priority-order: One PR's verdict checks merge conflicts, then unresolved threads, then failing CI, then merge gates, then pending checks, then readiness. (wp/policy.ts:218-236)
133. tier-major-stack-scan: Across a stack, each blocker tier is scanned over all PRs before the next tier, so an upstack conflict outranks bottom-PR CI. (wp/policy.ts:237-265; wp/policy.test.ts:155)
134. draft-gate-deferred-while-pending: A draft PR whose checks are still pending is reported as waiting, and the draft gate fires only after the checks settle. (wp/policy.ts:171-182; wp/policy.test.ts:201)
135. merge-gate-reasons: Closed-without-merge, draft (unless allowed) and changes-requested are terminal merge-gate blockers. (wp/policy.ts:160-182)
136. ready-requires-positive-proof: Ready means a clean merge state, no threads, clean CI with a GitHub allowance and an open non-rejected review state, and the types reject a ready verdict that lacks this proof. (wp/policy.ts:183-217; wp/types.ts:160-173; wp/types.compile.ts:75-85)
137. wait-attributed-to-pending-pr: A stack wait names the PR whose checks are actually pending, not the bottom PR. (wp/types.ts:233-248; wp/policy.ts:250-256; wp/policy.test.ts:178)
138. distinct-exit-codes: Exit 0 means ready, complete or status, 2 merge conflicts, 3 unresolved threads, 4 failing checks, 5 timeout, 6 merge gate, and 7 status-query failure. (wp/policy.ts:311-341, 403-408; wp/types.ts:305-346)
139. capped-exponential-query-backoff: A failed query retries after min(max(interval, 60) × 2^(n−1), 300) seconds, emitting a retry event. (wp/policy.ts:266-269, 384-410)
140. query-error-budget: A non-retryable error, or reaching the consecutive-failure budget, ends the watch with the status-query blocker, and any success resets the count. (wp/policy.ts:379-388)
141. deadline-capped-sleeps-and-timeouts: With a deadline set, every sleep is cut to the time left, and expiry yields a timeout verdict naming pending checks, unavailable status, or the queue frontier. (wp/policy.ts:352-378, 402-418, 687-693)
142. versioned-event-envelope: Every event carries a schema version, a rising sequence number, an observation timestamp, the mode, a kind and a terminal flag. (wp/policy.ts:270-310; wp/types.ts:259-277)
143. queue-capture-event: Queued mode first emits the captured queue in bottom-to-top order. (wp/policy.ts:718-722; wp/render.ts:135-136)
144. periodic-whole-stack-sweep-then-frontier-polls: Queued mode reads every unmerged PR on a sweep interval and otherwise polls only the lowest unmerged PR. (wp/policy.ts:560-575)
145. sweep-resumes-at-failed-read: A sweep drops a PR from its to-do list only after that PR's read succeeds, so a failed read is retried at the same PR. (wp/policy.ts:580-613; wp/policy.test.ts:235-256)
146. advance-event-without-sleep: When the frontier PR merges, an advance event names the next frontier and polling continues at once. (wp/policy.ts:679-686, 794-804; wp/policy.test.ts:338)
147. merge-queue-wait-ignores-upstack-pending: In queued mode a blocker-free frontier waits on the merge queue regardless of upstack pending checks. (wp/types.ts:238-242; wp/policy.ts:694-700)
148. deduplicated-wait-events: Identical consecutive wait events are emitted only once. (wp/policy.ts:701-711, 819-828)
149. status-table-rendering: The human rendering shows a PR, CI, review and merge table with full PR links and per-cell states (pending counts, failed counts, review automation running, open thread counts, draft, conflict). (wp/render.ts:4-54)
150. blocker-action-hints: Each human-rendered blocker states a next action, such as resolving conflicts, marking ready, or checking authentication and rearming, and lists failing checks and unresolved threads with their bot flags. (wp/render.ts:55-132)
151. leave-draft-note: A ready verdict reached under the allow-draft flag notes that the PR should stay a draft. (wp/render.ts:149-155)
152. watcher-test-suites-with-fake-reader: Behaviour is pinned by tests that run the policy, parsing and CLI against a fake GitHub reader and an injected clock. (wp/fakes.test-helper.ts:1-129; wp/policy.test.ts:46-482; wp/github.test.ts:33-498; wp/cli.test.ts:35-224)
153. compile-time-illegal-verdict-assertions: Expected-type-error lines prove that a refusal cannot pass as an allowance, clean CI cannot coexist with a refusal, ready cannot carry a blocker exit code, and ready needs proof. (wp/types.compile.ts:63-93)
154. strict-typecheck-script: A package script typechecks the watcher in strict mode without emitting output. (scripts/package.json:7; wp/tsconfig.json:1-13)
155. hash-keyed-dependency-install: The launcher hashes the package manifest and lockfile and installs dependencies only when the stored key differs or the CLI library is missing. (scripts/bootstrap.ts:17-33)
156. frozen-lockfile-install-verified: The install uses a frozen lockfile, surfaces its output on failure, and checks that the CLI library actually arrived. (scripts/bootstrap.ts:35-50)
157. restart-after-install: After a fresh install the launcher writes the new key and re-runs the original command, passing through its exit code. (scripts/bootstrap.ts:52-61; scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr:1-6)
158. pinned-cli-library: The argument-parsing library is pinned to an exact version, while the type packages float to latest and the lockfile records their resolved versions. (scripts/package.json:10-14; scripts/bun.lock:8-12)
159. read-only-worktree-audit: The audit lists every non-main git worktree with a suggested bucket and never deletes anything. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:2-5, 80-81)
160. explicit-merge-base-ref: The merged column checks against a ref given by flag, falling back to the remote default branch, then main, then master, with a warning when the flag is absent. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:7-11, 15-23, 33-39)
161. best-effort-base-fetch: The base ref is fetched first with an explicit refspec, and failure only warns that the column may be stale. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:41-48)
162. portable-stat-date-flags: The script detects GNU or BSD `stat` and `date` flags once. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:50-56)
163. pr-state-from-forge-cli: The user's PR states are fetched once from the forge CLI, with a fallback CLI, and become empty when neither works. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:58-70)
164. per-worktree-columns: Each row shows size, head age in days, ancestor-merged status, dirty state, remote state, PR number and state, and the last chat date. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:77-78, 83-109, 130-131)
165. squash-merge-caveat-via-pr-state: Ancestor checks catch only fast-forward or rebase merges, so PR state counts as the merge signal for squash merges. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:88-90, 125)
166. wip-versus-scratch-dirtiness: Tracked edits count as work in progress and only untracked files count as disposable scratch, each with a count. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:92-97)
167. remote-push-state: A branch is reported as detached, pushed, ahead by N, or having no remote branch. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:99-105)
168. last-chat-from-transcripts: The latest chat transcript that mentions the worktree path, matched exactly so prefixes do not collide, dates the last activity, and activity within four days counts as recent. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:72-75, 111-120)
169. prune-bucket-precedence: Buckets are assigned in order: hold for tracked work, hold for an open or draft PR, verify for a recent chat, safe for merged or any-PR, otherwise review. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:122-128)
170. sorted-by-size: Rows are sorted largest first. (scripts/worktree-audit.sh:132)

### Traits

- `skill-root-path-in-briefs` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours invokes another skill through the platform's skill mechanism, never by reading its file (`platform-skill-invocation`, `.claude/skills/mvp-mode/SKILL.md:30-31`), and reading a sibling by relative path was already rejected (`sibling-skill-by-relative-path`). A path in each brief serves only that rejected route.
- `principle-citation-in-reply` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: A principle is found cited or applied without its file having been read.; reason: Ours applies each principle whose situation holds (`.claude/skills/mvp-mode/SKILL.md:25`) but asks for no citation of it. The citation would let a reader check that a principle was applied, and the read-only guard keeps the citation honest; no failure of either kind is recorded yet.
- `task-start-goal-restatement` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: A run is found working toward a goal it misread, which a restatement at the start would have shown.; reason: Ours restates a goal when the person asks for it (`goal-and-problem-restatement`, the manual `restate` skill). Making it the first line of every task changes every reply, and no misread goal that it would have caught is recorded.
- `evidence-veto-stop` (new): absent; adopt, pending → doc:AGENTS.md; guide reword [U-02, U-04]; rewording: When evidence shows the requested change cannot meet its goal or would cause harm, show that evidence and ask before making the change.; reason: Prevents: An agent carrying out a requested change it already has evidence against, because the request read as authority to act. Lands in AGENTS.md, the Authority section, after the accuracy-over-agreement line. Upstream: SKILL.md:19.
- `goal-in-every-brief` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: A run is found working toward a goal it misread, which a restatement at the start would have shown.; reason: Our briefs state the outcome, owned paths, constraints, checks and pointers (`worker-brief-contents`, `AGENTS.md:49-50`). The user's goal behind the outcome is not asked for; it goes with the task-start restatement.
- `goal-opens-pr-why` (new): absent; reject; reason: `pr` opens its Summary with why the change exists (`pr/SKILL.md:28`), which is what a reviewer needs; the requester's goal behind it stays with the linked work item.
- `goal-opens-final-report` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: A run is found working toward a goal it misread, which a restatement at the start would have shown.; reason: Our final reports have their contents set (`final-report-contents`, `AGENTS.md:62-63`) and each playbook names its reply. Opening every one with the goal goes with the task-start restatement.
- `answerer-triage` (new): absent; reject; also in discovery (present); reason: Held already. `discovery` sorts each open question by who can answer it (the code, outside sources, a run, a routine pick, the owner) and puts to the owner only what the others cannot settle (`.claude/skills/discovery/SKILL.md:33-39`), and `AGENTS.md:9-10` asks only on a material ambiguity. A second copy in the router adds nothing.
- `prototype-settles-observable-fork` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours already sends a question a run can settle to a run (`answerer-triage`), and `prototype` is the unit when settling it needs something built. A standing rule to prototype rather than ask would add a build to forks a run or a read can settle.
- `autonomy-grant-decide-and-report` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: The owner defines a standing grant of full autonomy for a session. Ours has none, so these rows have nothing to attach to.; reason: Ours has no autonomy grant to scope this to.
- `operator-call-default-with-alternative` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: The owner defines a standing grant of full autonomy for a session. Ours has none, so these rows have nothing to attach to.; reason: Ours has no autonomy grant to scope this to.
- `named-gates-outlast-autonomy` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: The owner defines a standing grant of full autonomy for a session. Ours has none, so these rows have nothing to attach to.; reason: Ours already holds every consequential action for authorization (`AGENTS.md:11-12`) with no grant that could lift it; the rule matters only once such a grant exists.
- `own-words-answers-only` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours words each question so that a yes accepts the recommended answer (`yes-accepts-recommendation`, `discovery`), which is the short reply this forbids. We keep ours: a one-word yes to a stated recommendation is unambiguous.
- `data-shape-named-first` (new): absent; reject; reason: Held where it applies: the `model-the-domain` principle covers modelling the domain before logic, and `codebase-design` sketches types and shapes before code that crosses a function boundary. Before every line of code, including a one-line fix, it is ceremony (S-03).
- `design-before-cross-boundary-code` (new): absent; reject; reason: Held: `codebase-design` is the unit for shape decisions before code that crosses a function boundary, and the bug-fix and feature playbooks call it at that point. Whether options run in parallel is that skill's choice.
- `contested-design-multi-model-review` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours narrows this on purpose: run-proven adversaries start unasked only on a dispute raised by someone other than the lead, testable by a run and unsettled by evidence in hand (`contested-design-gate`, the feature playbook). A panel for every contested design would also spend runs on disputes a run cannot settle.
- `checkpoint-for-all-multistep-work` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours writes the checkpoint once, in the feature playbook's build step (`throughput-checkpoint`). Every multi-step task already copies its playbook's steps as todos, so a second plan of the same work adds a recipe without a better result (S-03).
- `same-surface-agent-repro` (new): absent; adopt, pending → create-verification-skill; guide ok [U-01]; reason: Prevents: A fix for an interface bug made without ever seeing the bug where the user saw it, so it lands on a cause the user's path never hit. Lands in create-verification-skill, SKILL.md, a new skill per the owner's ruling of 2026-11-05 (E). Wording at delivery: In the generated verification skill's use rules, require that the agent reproduce a reported interface bug itself, on the surface where it was seen, before any fix, handing that step to the person only when the surface needs something the agent cannot reach, such as their account or device, and saying which; the generator's own one-feature proof run needs no bug. Upstream: SKILL.md:31.
- `drive-shipped-surface` (new): absent; adopt, pending → create-verification-skill; guide ok [U-01]; reason: Prevents: A change to interface, editor or command-line behaviour claimed done from tests or a build, with the surface it ships on never driven. Lands in create-verification-skill, SKILL.md, a new skill per the owner's ruling of 2026-11-05 (E). Wording at delivery: In the generated verification skill's use rules, require that every change shipping behaviour on the surface it drives be exercised through that surface before it is called done. Upstream: SKILL.md:31.
- `finding-adjudication` (new): absent; reject; also in doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/implement.md (present), doc:AGENTS.md (variant), interrogate (variant), review (present); reason: Held already for every reviewer, bots included: `review` verifies each incoming finding against requirements, code and primary evidence and gives it a visible disposition, answering an incorrect one with a reason rather than a change (`.claude/skills/review/SKILL.md`).
- `separate-fix-for-broken-skill` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours files work found mid-task as a new bead linked to its origin (the Beads core rules, `discovered-from`) and builds a skill change on its own branch (`isolated-skill-build`). A pull request per skill fix assumes a review flow we do not run.
- `read-principle-before-applying` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours already tells where each principle lives (`.claude/skills/mvp-mode/SKILL.md:33-35`) and applies a principle whose situation holds (:25). Whether it is read before use goes with the citation row, deferred above, which would show it.
- `irreversible-writes-wait` (new): absent; reject; reason: Held in a wider form: `AGENTS.md:11-12` requires authorization before these and also before publishing, any message and scope expansion (`consequential-action-authorization`). The upstream lets the wider set go ahead, as the next row shows, so taking only this narrower list would add nothing.
- `irreversible-only-confirmation` (new): absent; reject; also in doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/pause-safely.md (variant), doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md (variant); reason: Already ruled on this trait (`2026-11-01-cursor_plugins-pstack-principles:091`): ours requires authorization for any message, publishing and scope expansion, while this lets team chat, ticket updates and eval launches go ahead unasked.
- `away-phrase-keeps-going` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: The owner decides how a run should behave when the request says the person is away. Today such a request does not start a run (`unattended-not-started`), and nothing here may depend on a session knowing whether its owner is present.; reason: The opposite of ours today: a request that says it will run unattended does not start (`stated-unattended-gate`, `unattended-not-started`), and an autonomous run needs a checkable exit (`exit-predicate-first`).
- `accuracy-over-agreement` (new): present in `doc:AGENTS.md`; adopt, delivered → doc:AGENTS.md; guide ok [U-04]; reason: AGENTS.md puts accuracy ahead of agreement and asks to point out errors and unchecked assumptions, which is the honest judgement this line asks for.
- `single-house-helper-type` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours picks each helper's vendor, model and type from the owner's roster per role (`owner-roster`) and uses the native helper only when it can run that model (`capable-native-subagent`). One house type would override both.
- `routed-skills-keep-helper-types` (new): absent; reject; reason: It only qualifies the house type rejected above; with no house type there is nothing to exempt.
- `no-playbook-in-delegate` (new): present in `mvp-mode`; adopt, delivered → mvp-mode; guide ok [U-07]; reason: The router says a delegated task never starts a playbook: the parent runs it, and the brief is its step.
- `background-every-dispatch` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours runs a worker in the background so the coordinator stays in dialogue with the person (`background-dispatch-for-dialogue`) and waits in the foreground when the next step depends on the result. Backgrounding every call, a short steer included, would leave the coordinator waiting for notices it could have had at once.
- `writable-helper-mode` (new): absent; reject; reason: Already ruled on this trait (`2026-11-01-batch-1:025`): a vendor tool limit, not a rule for us, and our read-only roles stay read-only.
- `pointer-only-subagent-briefs` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: The owner's review of deferred and rejected traits (`cr-r2pa.3.3`), as this trait was already deferred to it (`2026-10-30-mattpocock_skills-5beb35b:276`).; reason: Already deferred by the owner to a later review of the set (`2026-10-30-mattpocock_skills-5beb35b:276`); our briefs carry outcome, owned paths, constraints and checks beside the pointers (`AGENTS.md:49-50`).
- `role-model-config-line` (new): absent; reject; reason: Already ruled on this trait (`2026-11-03-batch-3:006`): model choice goes through `delegation` and the owner's roster, never a line in a unit (`owner-roster`).
- `vendor-default-role-models` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours takes every model from the owner's roster and asks the owner when no entry exists (`owner-roster`); fixed vendor defaults in a unit are what that forbids.
- `difficulty-tiered-model-choice` (new): absent; reject; reason: Model per role comes from the owner's roster (`owner-roster`) and effort from configuration (`configured-model-use`, `AGENTS.md:39-40`); a difficulty ladder in a unit would override both.
- `job-fit-helper-effort` (new): absent; reject; reason: Already ruled on this trait (`2026-11-06-batch-p1:189`): AGENTS.md says to use the configured models and reasoning effort (`configured-model-use`).
- `verification-on-worker-model` (new): absent; reject; reason: A fixed model for a kind of work is the roster's to set (`owner-roster`); ours also wants a reviewer from a different family than the author (`cross-family-review`), which a fixed worker model can break.
- `effort-change-keeps-family` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours adjusts neither: effort and model come from configuration and the roster (`configured-model-use`, `owner-roster`), and a value the vendor does not declare stops the dispatch (`validate-selection`) instead of being swapped for a near one.
- `rejected-model-swap` (new): absent; reject; reason: Already ruled on this trait (`2026-11-03-batch-3:007`): `delegation` asks the owner when no entry exists, and a value off the vendor's list stops the dispatch.
- `read-worker-output` (new): absent; reject; also in delegation (present); reason: Held already: `delegation` opens the diff or artifact a worker produced and holds it to its brief's evidence instead of relying on its summary (`.claude/skills/delegation/SKILL.md:67-69`). Writing one's own summary follows from that.
- `same-prompt-second-opinion` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours gets a second view from a reviewer of another family (`cross-family-review`) or, on request, a council with one neutral brief and a judge (`model-council`). Counting agreement as signal invites shared blind spots; we weigh evidence, not votes.
- `fresh-helper-per-round` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours does the opposite on purpose: a follow-up resumes the worker's own session (`session-resume-followup`, `.claude/skills/delegation/SKILL.md`), since its context is already loaded and a resume is cheap. A fresh helper per round re-reads everything.
- `distrust-interrupted-resume` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours trusts no summary in any case: the coordinator checks the worker's diff against its brief's evidence (`read-worker-output`). A dropped directive shows there, so a fresh helper adds cost without a better check.
- `draft-without-machine-patterns` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours sends a reply a person will read through `unslop`, and no case of that pass leaving the patterns in is recorded here. A second instruction for the same result is one more rule to keep with nothing it fixes.
- `one-thought-sentences` (new): absent; reject; reason: A fixed sentence shape for every reply is a style choice with no named failure; `unslop` already edits replies a person will read, and a reply's length is set by what it must say (U-05).
- `no-em-dash` (new): absent; reject; also in unslop (present); reason: Held by `unslop`, which every reply a person reads goes through; as in batch P1, a second copy adds nothing.
- `mid-sentence-colon-cut` (new): absent; reject; also in unslop (present); reason: Held by `unslop` (`mid-sentence-colon-cut`); a second copy in the router adds nothing.

- `impact-before-implementation` (new): absent; reject; reason: Held in substance: `principle-experience-first` treats whoever consumes the work as its user and explains impact from their side (`consumer-as-user`). The fixed order for every reply is style with no named failure.
- `only-seen-artifacts-cited` (new): absent; reject; reason: `AGENTS.md:15-16` already forbids fabricated citations. Limiting citations to this session's reads would also forbid citing a stable path the agent knows, which is not fabrication.

## skill:pstack/skills/poteto-help

Compared with `mvp-mode`; upstream tree hash `74d2f75606c45a357cb7ca58115398616d21bbadafbcd79c57e949c88c9edfb4`.

Suggested: delegation · purpose match: mvp-mode · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream answers questions about how to use its own pack and how to word a request. Ours has no help skill yet; the router answers what units exist and which fits. The owner's ruling of 2026-11-13 makes a new unit, working name `mvp-help`, for how to use this harness and advice to the person, which the adopt rows target.
Reason: Compared with mvp-mode: the unit that answers which unit fits and what exists. Suggested delegation by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. help-answers-without-starting-work: For a how-to question the skill answers, hands over a prompt the user can send, and links the source file, without starting the work itself, because a run costs real tokens. (SKILL.md:9)
2. work-request-runs-under-mode: A message that asks for work is done under the main mode skill, with one mention that a persistent mode keeps it on. (SKILL.md:11)
3. read-routed-file-before-quoting: The helper reads the file it routes to before quoting it, and trusts that file over its own map when they disagree. (SKILL.md:13)
4. give-public-copy-of-file: Links given to the user point at the public repository copy, not the installed path. (SKILL.md:13)
5. infer-need-else-one-choice-question: The need is inferred from context, and only if still unclear one multiple-choice question with five fixed options is asked, after which only the chosen section is answered. (SKILL.md:17-23)
6. state-checks-that-change-the-answer: The helper checks for the model-config rule, an app-driving verification skill and a formal verification skill, and for staleness of the last against its recorded sync commit, mentioning each only when it changes the answer. (SKILL.md:25-29)
7. one-time-model-setup-offer: When the model rule is missing and matters (new user, setup or cost question, model-dependent answer), the helper asks at most once per chat, bundled with any clarifying question, offering "now" or "later". (SKILL.md:31-34)
8. three-step-onboarding: Setup is install, run model configuration, then start a real task with the mode, a goal and a pass/fail check. (SKILL.md:38-40)
9. offer-to-word-first-prompt: The helper offers to word the user's first prompt using the prompting reference. (SKILL.md:42)
10. cost-reduction-guidance: For cost worries the helper explains where tokens go and how to cut them: a smaller budget, cheaper models, parent-model aliases, shorter panels, and saving the mode for work that needs rigor. (SKILL.md:44)
11. alternate-host-namespaced-install: On another host the pack installs with namespaced commands, and steps needing host-only features are skipped with a one-line note. (SKILL.md:46)
12. portability-caveat: Skills are readable elsewhere, but subagent-spawning workflows, persistent modes and loops may not work outside the primary host. (SKILL.md:48)
13. prompt-states-goal-and-done-not-skills: A good prompt states the goal and how to tell it is done, and does not list skills. (SKILL.md:52)
14. mode-persistence-explanation: The helper explains that a one-message attachment fades while a persistent custom mode stays every turn, and to restart the mode per task where modes are unavailable. (SKILL.md:54-58)
15. new-task-phrase-resets-playbook: Saying "new task" mid-chat makes the mode pick a fresh playbook. (SKILL.md:60)
16. user-subagents-can-use-house-type: Users can spawn their own subagents with the house subagent type to get the same style. (SKILL.md:60)
17. default-to-main-mode: The default recommendation is the main mode skill, and a specific skill is named only when the user wants more or less than the playbook gives, after reading it and with one example prompt. (SKILL.md:64)
18. unlisted-skill-routed-by-frontmatter: A sibling skill missing from the table is routed by reading its frontmatter description. (SKILL.md:103)
19. close-call-disambiguations: Fixed distinctions separate easily confused skill pairs (how versus why versus teach, arena versus swarm, interrogate versus blast-radius, recall versus ketchup, and the three long-run options). (SKILL.md:105-112)
20. out-of-pack-name-list: The helper says which commonly confused commands come from other packages or are built-ins, and that the coordinator playbook has no slash command. (SKILL.md:114-118)
21. design-questions-settled-in-code-first: A design question is settled first in code, through a prototype or design-exploration skill. (SKILL.md:133)
22. steer-by-principle-name: Users steer runs by naming a principle in their message instead of invoking it. (SKILL.md:135)
23. symptom-to-fix-troubleshooting-table: A table maps common run failures to fixes: a mode that faded, a question taken as the next step, a model change with no effect, high cost, a skill that did not load, agents overwriting each other, an overnight run that finished nothing, and success claimed from a green build. (SKILL.md:139-148)
24. isolate-parallel-agents: Parallel agents that overwrite each other get separate worktrees or separate cloud machines. (SKILL.md:146)
25. loop-needs-pass-fail-predicate: An unattended loop needs a check that can pass or fail, not a duration. (SKILL.md:147)
26. demand-real-proof-over-green-build: A reply that claims success from a green build is challenged for the real command, flow, stored value or profile. (SKILL.md:148)
27. short-answer-one-example-prompt: The reply leads with the answer, gives at most one example prompt in a code block adapted from the recipes file plus its link, and stays short unless the whole map was asked for. (SKILL.md:163)
28. prompt-includes-goal: A prompt says what is wrong or wanted. (references/prompting.md:7)
29. prompt-includes-pass-fail-done-check: A prompt carries a done check that can pass or fail, not "better" or a duration. (references/prompting.md:8)
30. prompt-names-proof-to-show: A prompt asks for real proof: command output, a video, the stored value, or before-and-after numbers. (references/prompting.md:9)
31. prompt-includes-known-evidence: A prompt includes symptoms, repro steps, logs or links the user already has. (references/prompting.md:10)
32. prompt-states-real-constraints: A prompt states constraints that change behaviour, such as repro first, no code changes yet, zero behaviour change, or review before proceeding. (references/prompting.md:11)
33. prompt-omits-the-how: A prompt says what to achieve, not how. (references/prompting.md:15)
34. prompt-omits-skill-sequence: A prompt does not list skills or steps, except to override one choice. (references/prompting.md:16)
35. withhold-cause-theory-until-restated: The user's cause theory is held back until the agent restates the problem, so it does not narrow the search. (references/prompting.md:17)
36. restate-noisy-report-first: For a noisy report, the agent first restates the underlying issue in plain words so a misreading shows before code. (references/prompting.md:21)
37. ask-for-a-case-not-a-summary: The agent is asked to argue for a choice (for example, that it fixes the cause), since a case is easier to check than a summary. (references/prompting.md:24)
38. never-take-first-design: The user asks for prototypes of several options, with screenshots or video for UI, and picks from evidence. (references/prompting.md:28)
39. prototypes-over-abstract-adversarial-review: Open questions are answered by prototypes, not by adversarial review of an abstract plan. (references/prompting.md:29)
40. docs-first-for-shared-api: For a shared package or API, the README or a tutorial is written first and becomes the target the code is checked against. (references/prompting.md:30)
41. plan-after-design-each-step-checked: The plan is requested only after the design settles, and each step ends in a check. (references/prompting.md:31)
42. terse-follow-ups: Short follow-ups such as "do it" or "keep going until done" are whole prompts once the chat holds the task. (references/prompting.md:35)
43. new-task-prefix-on-subject-change: "new task" starts a message that changes subject. (references/prompting.md:36)
44. announce-stepping-away: Saying the user is stepping away stops the agent asking questions. (references/prompting.md:40)
45. loop-predicate-as-checks: Done is written as checks every iteration can run and given to the loop as its predicate. (references/prompting.md:41)
46. fresh-worktree-off-named-base: Unattended work runs in a fresh worktree off a named base. (references/prompting.md:42)
47. pre-answer-stop-points: The user pre-answers what the agent would stop for, such as committing. (references/prompting.md:43)
48. request-decision-log: Unattended runs keep a decision log to audit later. (references/prompting.md:44)
49. explicit-stuck-exit: Unattended runs get an exit condition: stop and write up why if truly stuck after a few hours. (references/prompting.md:45)
50. one-line-steer-restate-goal: A drifting run is steered by restating the goal in one line. (references/prompting.md:49)
51. one-line-steer-name-principle: A drifting run is steered by naming the principle, which works because the agent read it and its reply names the decision it changed. (references/prompting.md:50-51)
52. read-dropped-findings-list: After an adversarial review, the user also reads its list of dropped findings. (references/recipes.md:36)
53. read-attention-section-first: In an overnight decision-log catch-up, the attention section is read first. (references/recipes.md:46)
54. approve-only-decision-changing-edits: Of the skill edits proposed after a run, only those that change a future decision are approved. (references/recipes.md:50)

Compared with `delegation`; upstream tree hash `3bba46e779c24a45db7602a8b47e3e184ca8215d812007ee5f2a114262ad9af1`.

Suggested: model-council · purpose match: delegation · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream writes the per-role model configuration through a guided run. Ours keeps that as the owner's roster, which `delegation` reads and validates; nothing of ours writes it yet. The owner's ruling of 2026-11-13 replaces upstream with a new guided setup unit, working name `setup-mvp-stack`, which the adopt rows target.
Reason: Compared with delegation: the holder of the roster and of model validation. The computed pick, model-council, shares only the judge-family rule, which is not this skill's job. Suggested model-council by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. always-applied-model-rule-file: The skill writes a single always-applied rule file in the user's rules directory that sets the model for each role. (SKILL.md:8, 39)
2. detect-model-slugs-from-subagent-tool: Available model slugs are taken from what the subagent tool accepts this session, and a models list or CLI is preferred for completeness when one exists. (SKILL.md:14)
3. ask-user-for-slugs-when-undetectable: If no slugs can be detected, the user is asked to paste the ones they can use. (SKILL.md:14)
4. never-write-unconfirmed-slug: A real slug is written only if confirmed available, and the two parent-model aliases are always valid. (SKILL.md:14, 35)
5. rerun-loads-existing-choices: On a rerun, the existing rule's budget line and role values are the starting choices, otherwise the defaults are. (SKILL.md:18)
6. drop-retired-role-lines: Lines for roles no longer in the schema are dropped and listed to the user. (SKILL.md:18, 31)
7. four-tier-budget-question: The user picks one of four labelled budgets (unlimited, large, medium, small) mapping to max, xhigh, high and medium reasoning, preferably via a structured question, with the current budget named. (SKILL.md:22-27)
8. budget-rewrites-effort-token: The chosen budget rewrites the effort token (the last token, or the one before a trailing `fast`) of every real slug, panel entries included. (SKILL.md:29)
9. effort-fallback-within-family: If the rewritten slug is unavailable, the same family's highest available effort at or below the target is used, otherwise the role is marked as needing a choice, and aliases never change. (SKILL.md:29)
10. keep-user-customised-roles-on-rerun: Roles the user changed by family, list or alias keep those changes on a rerun. (SKILL.md:29)
11. show-all-roles-and-confirm: Every role is shown with its model, undetected slugs are flagged, and the user accepts or changes specific roles from the detected models plus the aliases. (SKILL.md:31)
12. panel-list-length-sets-fan-out: For panel roles the value is a list, and one subagent runs per entry, aliases included. (SKILL.md:31, 47)
13. cross-judge-pool-rules: The cross-judge pool is an ordered preference list from which one judge is chosen, only from a family other than the parent's, and aliases never judge. (SKILL.md:31)
14. swarm-worker-default-model: The parallel-worker role sets every worker's model unless a race or comparison assigns models per arm. (SKILL.md:31)
15. validate-before-write-or-reask: Any chosen real slug not in the detected set stops the write and re-asks. (SKILL.md:35)
16. whole-file-overwrite-idempotent: The rule file is overwritten whole on each run so reruns stay idempotent. (SKILL.md:39)
17. budget-line-and-role-lines-format: The file records a budget line with label and effort, then one `role: value` line per role using the mode's role labels, and a deleted line falls back to the default. (SKILL.md:39-48)
18. default-role-model-table: The default code roles (feature and refactoring, bug-fix, perf-issue, hillclimb, how explorer, why investigators, reflect tooling, swarm workers) use `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast`. The default judgment roles (judgment and prose, hardest tasks, how explainer, why synthesizer, reflect judgment) use `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh`. Arena runners, the cross-judge pool, architect runners and interrogate reviewers each default to the pair of both. (SKILL.md:49-65)
19. applies-to-new-sessions-notice: The user is told the rule applies to new sessions and that rerunning updates it. (SKILL.md:70)
20. offer-verification-skill-once: If the project has no way to drive the real app for proof, the skill offers once to generate one and moves on without pushing on a no. (SKILL.md:74)
21. offer-formal-verification-skill-once: If the project has no formal verification skill, the skill offers once to generate one and moves on without pushing on a no. (SKILL.md:78)

Suggested: decision-trail · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream mines past chats to write a skill that captures the person's working style. `reflect` mines sampled sessions to propose edits to existing skills; it writes no persona.
Reason: Compared with reflect on purpose: the only unit of ours that reads past sessions to change skills. No row is present there; the computed pick, decision-trail, shares only the transcript privacy rule. Suggested decision-trail by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. detect-existing-mode-skill: The skill searches project and user skill directories recursively, personal category folders included, for an existing mode skill matching the user's handle. (SKILL.md:17)
2. update-vs-fresh-confirmation: If one exists, the skill confirms update (the default) or start fresh via a structured question, unless the user already said, and asks why before starting fresh. (SKILL.md:17-20)
3. incremental-mining-since-last-edit: In update mode, only history since the skill file's last commit date is mined. (SKILL.md:23)
4. delta-questions-in-update-mode: In update mode, the user is asked what changed or is missing, not what to capture from zero. (SKILL.md:24)
5. in-place-edit-preserving-uncontradicted: In update mode, the existing file is edited in place, keeping uncontradicted sections, revising ones with new evidence and adding sections only for new rules. (SKILL.md:25)
6. workspace-scoped-transcript-mining: Only the current workspace's transcript directory is mined, never a cross-workspace glob, to avoid reading unrelated private chats. (SKILL.md:29)
7. parallel-sliced-history-mining: Parallel subagents each mine one slice of recent history (for example 2 to 4 weeks in 3 slices), with effort and speed picked per the mode's subagent rules. (SKILL.md:31)
8. structured-pattern-return-with-pointers: Each mining subagent returns a short structured list of patterns with evidence pointers. (SKILL.md:31)
9. default-signal-checklist: Miners look for response preferences, delegation habits, verification posture, code and prose discipline, process conventions, and meta preferences about skills. (SKILL.md:33-38)
10. cross-slice-corroboration: A pattern seen in two or more slices is high-confidence, and a lone signal is usually dropped. (SKILL.md:40)
11. structured-multi-choice-interview: The user is asked one or two structured questions with 4 to 6 options, multi-select for categories, broad first then specific, then one free-form question, never a long question dump. (SKILL.md:44-48)
12. section-clustering-catalogue: Signals are grouped into the applicable sections from a fixed list: response style, autonomy, understand first, subagents, prose and code discipline, review and verify, process, and skills. (SKILL.md:52-61)
13. reference-skill-for-granularity-not-content: An existing mode skill is read for granularity only, and its content is not copied. (SKILL.md:63)
14. mode-skill-placement-rules: The path keeps an existing category, uses a personal category folder when the repo has one, else a top-level project mode folder, or the user's personal skills directory on request. (SKILL.md:69)
15. name-scoped-trigger-description: The description triggers on the user's name, their mode command and "work in their style", not on generic task words. (SKILL.md:71)
16. single-scalar-yaml-description: The description is one YAML scalar, quoted or folded when punctuation or wrapping needs it. (SKILL.md:72)
17. manual-invocation-by-default: The generated mode is manual-only by default unless the user wants it every turn. (SKILL.md:73)
18. iterate-draft-with-user-and-cut: The draft is shown to the user over several feedback rounds and cut hard. (SKILL.md:79)
19. land-via-worktree-and-pr: The skill is landed from a worktree off main with a commit and PR, never a direct push to main. (SKILL.md:83)
20. require-repeated-evidence: A preference is codified only after several instances, and a once-stated, later-contradicted one is noise. (SKILL.md:87)
21. operational-not-clever-prose: No restating other skills, metaphors or poetic prose for an agent reader. (SKILL.md:88)
22. reference-not-inline: Other skills and principle docs appear as path references, not pasted excerpts. (SKILL.md:89)
23. sections-only-for-non-default-rules: A section exists only if the user has a specific non-default rule there. (SKILL.md:90)
24. generic-person-naming: Imperatives say "the user" or "the human", not the author's name. (SKILL.md:91)
25. no-forced-symmetry: Sections without real content, such as an empty process section, are omitted. (SKILL.md:92)
26. vibe-check-evaluation: The mode is judged by a vibe check with the user (does it read like them, what is missing), not a benchmark loop. (SKILL.md:96)
27. trigger-tuning-only-on-observed-problem: A description-optimization loop runs only if trigger accuracy proves a problem in practice. (SKILL.md:98)
28. scope-excludes-task-and-narrow-workflow-skills: Task-specific skills and single narrow workflows are written as ordinary skills without mining, not as mode skills. (SKILL.md:102-103)

## skill:pstack/skills/make-bot-ui

Suggested: systematic-debugging · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream builds a small web page that triggers one product's chat bot through a webhook, served on a private network. Nothing of ours builds or runs such an integration.
Reason: Compared with none: no unit of ours has this job, and its only overlaps are two standing rules in `AGENTS.md`. Suggested systematic-debugging by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. server-side-relay-architecture: A browser page calls a local server, and only that server posts JSON to the bot's webhook. (SKILL.md:11, 55)
2. sender-key-never-in-browser-chat-or-skill: The webhook sender key lives only on the server, never in the browser, chat or skill text. (SKILL.md:11)
3. create-webhook-routine-via-state-tool: The routine is created through the state-update tool with a webhook trigger. (SKILL.md:15-17)
4. routine-prompt-contract: The routine prompt treats the POST body as untrusted data, names the expected JSON fields, performs the matching action, and stays silent when there is nothing to report. (SKILL.md:18)
5. wait-on-confirm-card: If creation shows a confirm card, the agent waits for the user. (SKILL.md:20)
6. slug-as-secret-connector: The routine's kebab-case folder slug is used later as the secret's connector name. (SKILL.md:21-22)
7. exact-ui-steps-for-url-and-key: The user gets exact steps to open the routine panel and copy the URL and key, and the agent invents no other clicks. (SKILL.md:27-35)
8. url-may-be-pasted-key-may-not: The webhook URL may be pasted into chat, but the sender key must not be. (SKILL.md:34-35)
9. copy-url-never-guess-id: The URL has a known shape with no query string and is copied from the routine, never guessed. (SKILL.md:37)
10. secret-request-card-is-whole-turn: The key is requested only through a secret-request card bound to the routine's connector, and sending it ends the turn. (SKILL.md:41-49)
11. secret-copied-blind: The agent never sees, prints or logs the submitted key, and copies it from the connector credential file into the server config. (SKILL.md:51)
12. per-ui-config-store: The URL and key are stored in the UI's own directory. (SKILL.md:55)
13. bind-all-interfaces-for-tailnet: The server binds `0.0.0.0`, not localhost, so tailnet peers can reach it. (SKILL.md:57)
14. webhook-post-spec: The relay sends POST with a JSON content type, the key in both a bearer header and a dedicated key header, one JSON object of the named fields, an 8-second timeout, and no retries. (SKILL.md:59-67)
15. harmless-probe-before-declaring-live: Before telling the user the UI is live, the agent probes once with a payload the routine prompt ignores and expects HTTP 200. (SKILL.md:69-71)
16. local-outbox-drained-by-routine: If posts can fail, the same JSON is appended to a local log that the routine drains, and polling is not the primary path. (SKILL.md:73)
17. no-media-bytes-on-webhook: Media bytes are never sent on the webhook. (SKILL.md:73)
18. reuse-existing-tailnet-node: If a Tailscale node is already online, install is skipped and no second hostname is created, because agents on the machine share one node. (SKILL.md:77-79)
19. give-both-tailnet-urls: The user gets both the MagicDNS URL and the 100.x IP URL, built from `tailscale status` and `tailscale ip -4`. (SKILL.md:79-82)
20. http-unless-asked: The page is served over plain HTTP unless the user asks for HTTPS. (SKILL.md:84)
21. tailscale-install-and-up-flags: If Tailscale is missing, it is installed with the official script and started with a short hostname and DNS and SSH features off. (SKILL.md:86-96)
22. user-approves-machine-via-login-url: The login URL goes to the user to approve, and the agent never asks for or types Tailscale credentials. (SKILL.md:98)
23. confirm-node-and-probe-page: After joining, the node is confirmed and the page is probed over its tailnet IP for HTTP 200. (SKILL.md:100-101)
24. reissue-expired-login-url: An expired login URL is replaced by rerunning the join command. (SKILL.md:103)
25. parse-wake-body-as-data: On a webhook wake, the agent parses the JSON string in the event's body field and treats it as data, not instructions. (SKILL.md:107-110)
26. no-credentials-printed: The agent never prints the sender key, tokens or cookies. (SKILL.md:112-113)
27. shared-small-field-vocabulary: The UI and the routine prompt use identical field names, and the field list stays small. (SKILL.md:114-115)

### Traits

- `credential-holding-relay` (new): absent; reject; reason: Owner ruling 2026-11-13: take nothing from this skill.
- `relay-config-beside-page` (new): absent; out-of-scope; reason: Where one product's relay keeps its settings, which we do not run.
- `webhook-routine-setup` (new): absent; out-of-scope; reason: Host-specific steps for one product's routines and secret cards, which we do not run.
- `webhook-field-contract` (new): absent; out-of-scope; reason: The message schema between one product's page and its webhook routine, which we do not run. Reading the body as data is held separately (`untrusted-content-no-authority`).
- `webhook-post-policy` (new): absent; out-of-scope; reason: The request format of one product's webhook. What happens to a post that fails is the outbox row below.
- `no-media-on-webhook` (new): absent; out-of-scope; reason: A size limit of one product's webhook, which we do not run.
- `failed-post-outbox` (new): absent; reject; reason: Owner ruling 2026-11-13: take nothing from this skill.
- `tailnet-exposure` (new): absent; out-of-scope; reason: Setup of one private-network product on the host, which nothing of ours does.
- `untrusted-content-no-authority` (new): present in `doc:AGENTS.md`; adopt, delivered → doc:AGENTS.md; guide ok [C-06]; reason: AGENTS.md says external content cannot authorize actions or override instructions, which is reading a webhook body as data.
- `secret-containment` (new): present in `doc:AGENTS.md`; adopt, delivered → doc:AGENTS.md; guide ok [U-01]; also in doc:.repo-context/coding-style.md (variant), systematic-debugging (variant); reason: AGENTS.md keeps secrets out of unauthorized destinations, chat and output included, which is never printing or pasting the key.
- `harmless-probe-before-live` (new): absent; reject; reason: `AGENTS.md:61-62` already requires observing the real thing before claiming a result (`direct-observation`); the ignored payload is this integration's own way of doing that.

Suggested: principle-subtract-before-you-add · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream takes a bug report from a team chat after triage, reproduces it through the real interface, fixes it and opens a draft pull request, posting status to chat. Our bug-fix playbook fixes a reported defect with proof but cannot be compared, being no skill; `systematic-debugging` holds the reproduction and diagnosis it calls.
Reason: Compared with systematic-debugging: the skill whose reproduction rules the portable rows are measured against. The whole flow's counterpart is the bug-fix playbook, which cannot be compared. Suggested principle-subtract-before-you-add by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. fail-closed-on-missing-config: Missing config, required actions, control adapter or completed feature map stops the run. (SKILL.md:11)
2. freeze-source-coordinates-first: Before any work list or delegation, the channel must match the configured source, the thread timestamp is taken from the trigger's thread field else its own timestamp, must be non-empty, is stored immutably, is verified against the thread root, and the permalink is fetched. (SKILL.md:15, 34-43)
3. never-substitute-coordinates: Source coordinates are never replaced by a reply, operations or status timestamp. (SKILL.md:45)
4. never-post-source-root: No root message is ever posted in the source channel. (SKILL.md:16)
5. per-post-parent-preflight: Before every source-thread post, the agent rereads the thread, confirms the parent exists, is not deleted and is still in the source channel, sends with both coordinates, and rereads to confirm the post is a reply. (SKILL.md:17, 47-52)
6. no-fallback-on-failed-preflight: If any preflight check fails, nothing is posted, with no retry at the root or in another channel. (SKILL.md:54)
7. coordinator-sole-chat-poster: Only the coordinating agent posts to chat. (SKILL.md:18, 244)
8. read-only-analysis-workers: Delegated analysis workers are read-only and return only findings or media notes. (SKILL.md:19, 246-254)
9. isolated-fix-worker-or-coordinator-edits: A fix-phase code worker may edit only if its environment provably lacks chat credentials and write actions, otherwise the coordinator edits. (SKILL.md:20, 256)
10. explicit-chat-write-ban-in-child-prompts: Every child prompt explicitly forbids the named chat-posting actions and all other chat writes. (SKILL.md:21, 159, 256)
11. no-posting-capability-to-children: Children never receive a chat token, posting instructions, posting coordinates or permission to report externally, and a child that needs chat write access is not launched. (SKILL.md:22-23)
12. utility-bots-are-evidence-not-owners: Utility bots are evidence sources and do not own the fix unless a person explicitly delegated it to them. (SKILL.md:24)
13. discriminating-symptom-twice-via-real-ui: A repro counts only if the exact discriminating symptom appears twice through real UI interaction. (SKILL.md:25, 171-179)
14. inspection-confirms-never-injects: State inspection may confirm an observation but must never inject or force the symptom. (SKILL.md:26)
15. no-repro-no-fix: Without a confirmed repro, no fix is authored. (SKILL.md:27)
16. existing-artifact-switches-to-verify: An existing PR or commit switches the run to verify mode, and nothing is authored over it. (SKILL.md:28, 99, 220-224)
17. github-link-form: PR links use github.com URLs in the configured public form. (SKILL.md:29, 293)
18. artifacts-out-of-source-control: Captures, recordings, logs and tokens stay out of source control. (SKILL.md:30)
19. trusted-triage-marker-gate: The run waits silently for the configured verdict window and accepts a verdict only from the configured triage identity, as a reply in the source thread, with exactly one configured marker. (SKILL.md:58-64)
20. proceed-only-bug-or-performance: Work proceeds only for bug or performance markers, capturing any tracker URL, and stops silently for other, missing, untrusted, conflicting or timed-out verdicts. (SKILL.md:66-76)
21. fixed-marker-format: Verdict markers have a fixed bracketed form with an optional `tracker=` URL. (SKILL.md:66-74)
22. reread-thread-before-work: The thread is reread immediately before work starts. (SKILL.md:82)
23. yield-to-human-fix-claim: The run stops when a person claims the fix, gives a concrete implementation plan, or asks another agent to implement or open a PR. (SKILL.md:84-86)
24. diagnosis-requests-are-not-ownership: Bot summaries, log or ticket lookups, requests to diagnose or reproduce, and unaccepted cause hypotheses do not count as fix ownership, judged by the action requested. (SKILL.md:88-95)
25. concrete-fix-artifact-definition: A fix artifact is an open PR or merged commit found via thread, tracker, history or PR search, and a bare claim is not one. (SKILL.md:99-101)
26. do-not-race-owner-without-artifact: If a person owns the work but has no artifact yet, the run stops. (SKILL.md:103)
27. optional-operations-thread-only-root: If an operations channel is configured, one root status message there is the only root post allowed, with coordinates stored separately from the source. (SKILL.md:107-109)
28. fixed-status-vocabulary: Status uses short configured strings: reproducing, could not reproduce, blocked, reproduced, verifying existing fix, attempting bounded fix, draft PR opened, fix did not land. (SKILL.md:111-120)
29. narrow-bot-token-never-to-workers: An optional bot token is used only for a configured narrow gap such as editing the status message, prefers built-in chat actions, and never reaches a worker. (SKILL.md:122)
30. no-ops-channel-status-to-run-output: Without an operations channel, detailed status goes to the run output, never to a source root post. (SKILL.md:124)
31. feature-map-section-required: The matching feature-map section must be read before driving the app, and a missing section blocks the run instead of inventing a path or selector. (SKILL.md:128-130)
32. seven-adapter-capabilities-required: The control adapter must bring up the app, navigate mapped features and states, drive real UI, inspect without mutating, screenshot, record, and clean up, or the run is blocked. (SKILL.md:132-142)
33. no-proxy-repro: A screenshot, unit test, state mutation or source reading never counts as a UI repro. (SKILL.md:142)
34. report-study-fields: The agent collects action path, expected and observed behaviour, discriminating state, frequency, version and environment, attachments and error signatures, and candidate code area. (SKILL.md:146-157)
35. inspect-media: Screenshots and video are inspected. (SKILL.md:159)
36. parallel-read-only-research-workers: Read-only parallel workers may handle code history, test ideas, blast radius and media, each with one narrow question. (SKILL.md:159)
37. trace-and-competing-hypotheses: The action is traced through the code, regression history is checked, and competing cause hypotheses are formed along with the evidence that would separate them. (SKILL.md:161)
38. confirm-correct-target-via-stable-markers: Before acting, the agent confirms app, workspace, account, data set and feature state using stable markers, not window order or title. (SKILL.md:167)
39. name-correct-and-broken-end-states: Before calling a repro, the correct and broken final states are named and the point of divergence is reached. (SKILL.md:173-175)
40. reset-for-independent-second-attempt: State is reset enough that the second attempt is independent. (SKILL.md:177)
41. real-state-cross-check: A real state value is cross-checked when possible. (SKILL.md:179)
42. setup-steps-are-not-the-bug: Expected dialogs, loading states or setup steps are not the bug, and the captured state must separate correct from broken. (SKILL.md:181)
43. repro-budget-clean-outcomes: Within the repro budget, the outcome is either a clean "could not reproduce" or "blocked" naming the missing capability. (SKILL.md:183)
44. repro-evidence-bundle: A successful repro keeps a full-path recording, a broken-state screenshot and a step note in the configured temporary directory. (SKILL.md:187-192)
45. independent-media-review-gate: A read-only media reviewer answers whether the evidence visibly shows the broken state, and a no or unsure means the repro is not confirmed. (SKILL.md:194-196)
46. detail-in-ops-concise-in-source: Detailed evidence goes only to the operations thread, and the source update stays brief. (SKILL.md:198)
47. ops-status-first: The operations status updates before any source reply. (SKILL.md:202)
48. silent-source-on-failure: For "could not reproduce" or "blocked", nothing is posted to the source thread. (SKILL.md:204)
49. one-unprompted-repro-reply: A confirmed repro gets at most one preflighted source reply saying it reproduced, linking the evidence thread and tracker, with at most three findings and no default owner ping. (SKILL.md:206-212)
50. attachments-only-in-thread-within-retention: Evidence is attached only when it stays in the source thread and retention policy allows it. (SKILL.md:214)
51. rejection-window-before-fix: The fix phase waits out a configured rejection window, and one valid correction triggers one corrected repro. (SKILL.md:216)
52. verify-existing-fix-twice-each-side: Verifying an existing fix shows the symptom on the baseline and its absence on the patched build, each twice through real UI. (SKILL.md:222)
53. bounded-fix-qualification-gate: A fix is attempted only when the repro is plainly confirmed, media review confirmed it, no artifact appeared, no one claimed it during the window, runtime evidence names the root cause, the change fits the fix budget and scope, and the adapter can run both builds. Otherwise the run keeps the repro report and stops. (SKILL.md:228-238)
54. coordinator-owns-diff-commits-pr: The coordinator owns the final diff review, commits and PR. (SKILL.md:244)
55. coordinator-verifies-delegated-edit: The coordinator reviews any delegated edit and runs or checks the required tests, keeping the edit itself when isolation is uncertain. (SKILL.md:256)
56. runtime-confirmed-mechanism: The mechanism is confirmed with runtime evidence and competing hypotheses are eliminated before editing. (SKILL.md:258)
57. smallest-root-cause-change: The fix addresses the root cause with the smallest justified change. (SKILL.md:260)
58. test-first-when-cheap: When a cheap local test target exists the failing test is written first, otherwise the reason for skipping is stated. (SKILL.md:262-263)
59. no-unrelated-cleanup: Unrelated cleanup stays out. (SKILL.md:264)
60. stop-on-budget-overrun: Work stops if the change exceeds the configured effort or risk budget. (SKILL.md:265)
61. after-proof-mirrors-baseline: On the patched build, the same path runs twice, the broken state is gone, the expected state appears, an after recording and screenshot are captured, and the same state value is cross-checked. (SKILL.md:269-278)
62. compile-or-tests-not-after-evidence: A compile, unit test, review or plausible diff is not after-evidence. (SKILL.md:280)
63. focused-tests-and-blast-radius-smoke: Focused tests run, then a smoke of nearby states, inputs, permissions, platforms and failure paths, and any remaining regression means no PR. (SKILL.md:282)
64. pre-pr-diff-and-secret-review: Before the PR, the final diff is reviewed for unrelated changes and secrets and the repository's required checks run. (SKILL.md:288-289)
65. small-ordered-commits: Commits are small and ordered when the repository allows. (SKILL.md:290)
66. draft-pr-never-merge-or-deploy: The workflow opens only a draft PR and never merges or deploys. (SKILL.md:291)
67. pr-links-tracker-issue: The PR links the tracker issue with the tracker's own syntax. (SKILL.md:292)
68. pr-body-contents: The PR body carries repro steps, root cause, test results, before-and-after evidence and blast-radius checks. (SKILL.md:294)
69. honest-pr-failure-reporting: If PR creation fails, success is not claimed, branch state goes in the run output, and the status says the fix did not land. (SKILL.md:297)
70. success-reported-in-ops-only: On success, the status updates and one ops-thread reply links the PR, with no extra source posts. (SKILL.md:299)
71. bounded-follow-up-window: For one follow-up window, the run answers direct questions from existing evidence, applies one concrete correction with one rerun, stays out of side chatter, and stops when asked. (SKILL.md:303-308)
72. always-run-cleanup-with-retention: Adapter cleanup always runs, and artifacts are kept only as long as retention allows. (SKILL.md:310)
73. configured-adapter-and-map-paths: The adapter is a configured skill name, and the feature map is a filled copy kept outside the pack and pointed to by config. (references/control-adapter.md:3-7)
74. adapter-fail-closed: An absent, ambiguous or incomplete adapter, map or capability stops repro and fix work. (references/control-adapter.md:9)
75. bring-up-contract: Bring-up takes repo, revision, mode, environment requirements, artifact directory and map path, and returns a session id, how the target was confirmed, stable markers, process details and missing capabilities. (references/control-adapter.md:13-31)
76. distinguish-target-from-lookalikes: The adapter must tell the target app from similar windows, shells or production instances. (references/control-adapter.md:33)
77. real-user-action-set: UI driving uses only real user actions (click, type, keys, scroll, drag, resize, in-app navigation), each returned with its observed state change. (references/control-adapter.md:35-49)
78. semantic-selectors-coordinates-after-screenshot: Roles, labels and stable selectors are preferred, and coordinates are used only after a fresh screenshot. (references/control-adapter.md:47)
79. no-symptom-injection: Internal state, hidden methods, direct storage writes and DOM injection are never used to create the symptom. (references/control-adapter.md:51)
80. mapped-feature-driving-surface: The adapter navigates each mapped feature, invokes its named actions, exercises the standard UI states, arranges preconditions through safe test controls, resets for a second attempt, and captures the map's named evidence. (references/control-adapter.md:53-64)
81. stable-selector-policy: Selectors use roles, accessible names, ARIA relations, component markers or purpose-named data attributes, never generated classes, hashes, child indexes or DOM position. (references/control-adapter.md:66)
82. preconditions-are-not-symptom-permission: Arranging a precondition never licenses injecting the reported symptom. (references/control-adapter.md:68)
83. read-only-inspection-contract: Inspection (accessibility tree, view hierarchy, process state, logs, network status, debug state) is read-only, and any state-changing query must be a real user action. (references/control-adapter.md:70-83)
84. screenshot-contract: Screenshots return path, time, app marker and an expected-content description, and show enough chrome to prove the correct app. (references/control-adapter.md:85-96)
85. recording-contract: Recordings span the full path, return path, times, region and omitted overlays, and must show the discriminating final state. (references/control-adapter.md:98-109)
86. cleanup-contract: Cleanup stops created processes, removes disposable profiles, workspaces, created fixtures, ports, tunnels and expired captures, reports what was stopped, removed, retained or left, and never deletes user work. (references/control-adapter.md:111-125)
87. adapter-behaviour-rules: The adapter reports capabilities and drivable map sections up front, uses identical inputs for baseline and patched builds, surfaces startup failures, bounds retries, keeps secrets and captures out, supports a reset between attempts, and avoids production changes without a configured safe action. (references/control-adapter.md:129-139)
88. environment-translation-before-blocking: Before declaring an environment block, the defect is restated without platform nouns, and a translated attempt is used only if it tests the same behaviour and is labelled as translated, never as an exact repro. (references/control-adapter.md:141-151)
89. genuine-block-categories: Hardware prompts, OS permission dialogs, device-only APIs and unavailable account states may be real blocks. (references/control-adapter.md:153)
90. nine-step-harmless-setup-check: Before enabling repro, a nine-step harmless run (bring up, confirm marker, load a section, navigate, exercise a disposable state, inspect, screenshot, record, clean up) must fully pass with no source chat post. (references/control-adapter.md:155-169)
91. artifact-owns-the-fix: In verify mode the existing artifact owns the fix, and the run neither edits it nor authors a competing patch or PR. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:5)
92. concrete-artifact-required: A verifiable artifact is an open PR with relevant code, a merged PR or a matching merged commit, and claims, tracker status, branch names or hypotheses are not enough. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:9-15)
93. artifact-selection-rule: Among several artifacts, the one linked from the thread or tracker wins, otherwise the closest match with a stated reason. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:17)
94. isolated-checkout-for-verification: Verification uses an isolated worktree or clean checkout without overwriting user changes. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:21)
95. record-verification-inputs: The run records baseline and patched revisions, the artifact URL and the shared build and environment inputs. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:23-28)
96. baseline-revision-choice: The baseline is the open PR's base branch, or the revision just before a merged fix when it builds and shows the old behaviour. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:34-36)
97. no-double-baseline-no-claim: If the baseline does not show the symptom twice, no claim that the fix works is made. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:38-47)
98. patched-run-same-environment-twice: The patched build runs with the same environment and data, twice, showing the broken state gone and the expected state present, with the same captures and state check. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:49-57)
99. running-patched-app-required: After-evidence must come from the running patched app, not compilation or tests. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:59)
100. confirmed-outcome-actions: Confirmed means baseline reproduces twice and patched resolves twice, which yields a verified status, an artifact link, one preflighted source reply with before and after, and no PR. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:63-71)
101. insufficient-fix-outcome-actions: A symptom on both builds yields a "reproduced but not fixed" status, an artifact link saying it did not resolve, the normal repro update if unused, and no competing PR. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:73-80)
102. inconclusive-outcome-actions: A missing baseline, an unrunnable patch or weak evidence yields no success claim, a statement of which half failed, results kept in ops or run output, and no source post unless directly asked. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:82-89)
103. verification-cleanup-restore: Both builds stop, temporary profiles and captures are removed per retention, and the repository returns to its prior state without losing user work. (references/verify-existing-fix.md:93)
104. user-level-feature-map: The map describes features from the user's point of view, and internals and code paths are discovered at runtime, not frozen in it. (references/feature-map.example.md:3)
105. refresh-safe-map-copy: The map is copied outside the pack and pointed to by config, so pack refreshes never overwrite it. (references/feature-map.example.md:5)
106. per-feature-section-template: Each feature section records its purpose, the user path and shortcut, adapter actions with expected results plus a reset, stable selectors, states to exercise, preconditions (auth, data, permissions, flags, services), evidence and cross-check, and gotchas. (references/feature-map.example.md:7-57)
107. mark-inapplicable-states: States that do not apply to a feature are marked as such. (references/feature-map.example.md:38)
108. map-completeness-checklist: A checklist confirms every reproducible feature has a section with path, actions and reset, stable selectors only, covered states, explicit preconditions, explicit evidence, listed wrong surfaces and translations, and no implementation details. (references/feature-map.example.md:195-205)
