Purpose: Upstream installs a chat-automation pack into a repository and creates its two automations. Nothing of ours installs or runs chat automations.
Reason: Compared with none: no unit of ours has this job. Suggested systematic-debugging by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. dormant-pack-read-by-path: The automation pack ships dormant, is never registered as slash skills, and its files are read directly from the copied repository path. (SKILL.md:9-11, 65)
2. no-automation-writes-until-asked: No automation is created or updated until the user explicitly asks. (SKILL.md:15)
3. no-secrets-in-files-or-prompts: Secret values never go in plugin files, prompts or committed configuration. (SKILL.md:15)
4. copy-before-config: The pack copy and dependency enablement come before asking for configuration or invoking the automation-creation skill. (SKILL.md:19)
5. ask-target-repository: The user names which repository runs the automations. (SKILL.md:21)
6. additive-merge-copy: The whole pack is merged into the destination path, creating it if absent and copying each file to the same relative path. (SKILL.md:23-26)
7. never-delete-destination-only-files: Install or refresh never deletes files that exist only in the destination. (SKILL.md:27)
8. user-owned-config-kept-outside: User-owned config, feature maps and routing maps live outside the pack destination and are never overwritten. (SKILL.md:28)
9. diff-merge-changed-managed-files: A differing pack-managed file is diff-reviewed and merged without discarding local edits, and ambiguous ownership stops for the user. (SKILL.md:29)
10. verify-copied-contents: The destination is checked for the entry doc, setup file, both operational files, their references and the templates. (SKILL.md:30)
11. in-place-run-still-verifies: If setup is already reading from the destination, the copy counts as done but verification still runs. (SKILL.md:32)
12. enable-pack-in-project-settings: The pack is enabled in the project settings JSON by merging one entry, preserving other settings, plugins and JSONC comments, changing only the enabled flag if present, then validating the file. (SKILL.md:34-46)
13. fresh-agent-project-scope-dependency-check: A fresh agent in the target repo must resolve the listed shared skills and principles from project scope, and session or user-scope resolution does not count. (SKILL.md:48-61)
14. stop-on-unresolved-dependencies: If project-scope install is unavailable or any dependency fails to resolve, setup stops and explains. (SKILL.md:63)
15. commit-before-enable-notice: The user is told settings, pack and referenced config must be committed before enabling, and the agent does not commit them unless asked. (SKILL.md:67)
16. live-prompts-reference-committed-paths: Live automation prompts read committed operational files by stable repo-relative paths, never a plugin cache path or copied contents. (SKILL.md:69, 92, 181-182)
17. user-owned-config-copies: The config and feature-map examples are copied to user-owned locations outside the pack (project or user scope), and the examples are never edited. (SKILL.md:73-88)
18. one-section-per-user-facing-feature: The feature map has a section for every user-facing feature the automation may reproduce, at user level without implementation details. (SKILL.md:86)
19. committed-file-or-paraphrase: A fresh checkout reads committed secret-free files when possible, otherwise values are paraphrased into the prompt, and a file is referenced only after the creation skill confirms it is committed. (SKILL.md:90)
20. required-choices-checklist: Setup asks for source channel, optional ops channel, repo and branch, triage identity, tracker type and fields, tracker adapter, optional routing path, control skill, feature-map path, status emojis, PR URL format, polling and effort budgets, and model slugs for triage, repro, code and media review. (SKILL.md:96-110)
21. available-model-slugs-only: Model slugs must be ones the user can actually select, never guessed or carried over from a private default. (SKILL.md:112)
22. required-values-explicit-or-fail: Source channel, triage identity, repository, tracker adapter, control skill and feature map must be explicit, or setup fails. (SKILL.md:114)
23. integration-capability-checklists: Triage needs channel and thread read, thread reply, attachment download and full tracker access. Repro needs thread read and reply, optional ops post and edit, repo history, draft-PR creation and the control adapter. (SKILL.md:120-134)
24. built-in-chat-actions-first-narrow-token: Built-in chat actions are preferred, and an optional bot token fills only a narrow gap, stored in a secret manager or environment rather than YAML. (SKILL.md:136)
25. no-undocumented-endpoints: Undocumented integration endpoints are never used. (SKILL.md:138)
26. routing-map-preparation: For reroutes or pings, the routing example is copied outside the pack with all placeholders replaced. (SKILL.md:142-145)
27. pings-off-and-narrowly-allowed: Owner pings default off and are allowed only for a configured feature owner or a confirmed likely regression author. (SKILL.md:146-147)
28. no-map-no-guessed-destination: Without a routing map, triage may classify but never guesses a destination or owner. (SKILL.md:149)
29. adapter-capability-verification-gate: The named control skill must prove it can bring up the app, navigate every mapped feature through real UI, exercise mapped states, inspect without forcing, screenshot, record and clean up, or the repro automation stays disabled. (SKILL.md:153-165)
30. first-time-or-existing-branch: The user is asked whether automations are new or existing, and the pack's entry doc is the primary intent source for both. (SKILL.md:169-171)
31. one-automation-at-a-time: Automations are created one at a time, each finishing its editor handoff before the next. (SKILL.md:175, 187)
32. creation-request-assembly: Each creation request combines the entry doc, the finished config and the template intent into a complete natural-language request, and the template is read as secondary material. (SKILL.md:179-180)
33. delegate-discovery-and-approval-to-creation-skill: The built-in creation skill discovers channels, repo and integrations, confirms committed files, shows its draft, gets approval, asks readiness and opens the editor, and setup does not duplicate that work. (SKILL.md:183-187, 214)
34. triage-automation-intent-spec: The triage automation is named, follows its operational file every run, triggers on each new top-level report, reads and replies only in-thread, uses the tracker, classifies, inspects evidence, traces cause, dedupes, creates only clear new bugs, and ends one thread-only verdict with a marker and optional tracker URL. (SKILL.md:189-198)
35. repro-automation-intent-spec: The repro automation follows its operational file, uses the same trigger, repo and branch, replies in-thread only, includes PR, tracker, adapter and map requirements, waits for a trusted marker, reproduces twice via real UI, verifies existing fixes without authoring over them, and opens a draft PR only after confirmed repro, proof and checks. (SKILL.md:200-212)
36. existing-automations-via-editor-checklist: Because the creation skill cannot update automations, existing ones get a field-by-field checklist for the user to update in the editor, with no replacements or duplicates created. (SKILL.md:218-242)
37. creation-boundary: No direct backend service or tool, no draft-carrying browser URL and no protocol deep link, and the only creation path is the reviewed editor handoff. (SKILL.md:246)
38. enable-only-after-thread-safety-test: Neither automation is enabled until the thread-safety test passes after the editor save. (SKILL.md:248)
39. thread-safety-test-preflight: The test uses a test channel or harmless report, and it first confirms everything is committed on the automation's branch and both prompts point at their exact files, stopping otherwise. (SKILL.md:252-254)
40. seven-thread-safety-checks: The test checks that triage stores the root timestamp and posts one reply, the verdict has one marker, repro trusts only the triage identity, coordinates stay fixed, no root message appears, workers cannot write to chat, and missing coordinates or failed preflight produce no post or ticket. Normal traffic is enabled only when all seven pass. (SKILL.md:256-266)

## skill:pstack/automations/benny/skills/triage-issue-reports

Compared with `triage`; upstream tree hash `dcca688d8d2f3ddd586274f67aea96d04c6175f730706ecef15536412a430c5d`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |
|---|---|---|

| doc:.repo-context/coding-style.md | 1 |  |
| doc:AGENTS.md | 1 |  |
| grilling | 1 |  |
| systematic-debugging | 1 |  |
| triage | 0 | yes |

Suggested: discovery · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream classifies one bug report posted in a team chat, files a tracker issue for a clear new bug and replies in the thread. Our `triage` decides on items already filed in Beads; it files nothing and posts nowhere.
Reason: Compared with triage: the same kind of decision on incoming work and the unit the duplicate rows land in, though the source and output differ. The computed pick, discovery, shares only the rule to look facts up before asking. Suggested discovery by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. triage-scope-no-repro-or-fix: The run classifies one report, posts one verdict and files only clear new bugs, never reproducing or fixing. (SKILL.md:9)
2. triage-fail-closed-on-config: Missing, malformed or incomplete config stops the run with no post and no tracker write. (SKILL.md:11)
3. immutable-source-coordinates: The source channel and root thread coordinates never change during the run. (SKILL.md:15, 42)
4. never-post-source-root-triage: The run never posts a root message in the source channel. (SKILL.md:16)
5. no-other-channel-broadcast-dm-or-new-thread: The run never posts to another channel, broadcasts a reply, sends a DM or starts a replacement thread. (SKILL.md:17)
6. preflight-before-tracker-write-and-verdict: The source parent is preflighted before any tracker write and again immediately before the verdict. (SKILL.md:18, 202)
7. uncertain-parent-stops-all-writes: A missing, deleted, inaccessible or uncertain parent stops the run with no writes. (SKILL.md:19)
8. single-verdict-no-progress-narration: One substantive verdict is posted, with no progress messages. (SKILL.md:20)
9. coordinator-only-poster-triage: Only the coordinator posts to chat. (SKILL.md:21)
10. read-only-credentialless-workers: Workers return findings only, are read-only, and get no chat credentials or write actions. (SKILL.md:22)
11. chat-write-ban-in-child-prompts-triage: Every child prompt forbids the named chat-posting actions and all other chat writes. (SKILL.md:23)
12. coordinator-does-work-without-isolation: If worker isolation cannot enforce those limits, the coordinator does the work itself. (SKILL.md:24)
13. issue-must-link-back: No issue is created that cannot link to the source thread. (SKILL.md:25)
14. prefer-no-ticket: No ticket is preferred over a guessed or duplicate one. (SKILL.md:26)
15. freeze-coordinates-protocol: Before any work list or delegation, the channel id is read and must match config, the thread timestamp comes from the trigger's thread field else its own timestamp and must be non-empty, both are stored immutably, the root is verified, and a stable permalink is fetched. (SKILL.md:32-40)
16. read-full-thread-before-deciding: The root and all current replies are read before deciding. (SKILL.md:46)
17. report-capture-fields: The run captures reporter wording, version, build, environment and platform, expected and observed behaviour, frequency and trigger, error signature, existing links, and any statement that someone is already fixing it. (SKILL.md:48-57)
18. inspect-every-relevant-attachment: Screenshots are read at full useful resolution, video is reviewed for the correct-to-broken transition, and logs and traces are read for signatures. (SKILL.md:59-63)
19. narrow-read-only-media-worker: Specialist media review goes to a read-only worker with a narrow question that returns findings only. (SKILL.md:64)
20. admit-unreadable-attachments: An unreadable attachment is named as such in the verdict, never guessed at. (SKILL.md:65)
21. use-thread-evidence-before-asking: Evidence already in the thread is used before asking the reporter for more. (SKILL.md:67)
22. bounded-cause-trace-before-routing: Before choosing an owner, a bounded pass traces the action-to-result code path, checks whether the symptom belongs there or below, checks recent changes for regressions, looks for existing fixes, and separates facts from hypotheses. (SKILL.md:71-77)
23. trace-depth-sufficient-for-routing: The trace need not find the full root cause but must be strong enough to avoid misrouting a visible symptom. (SKILL.md:79)
24. unreadable-repo-conservative-classification: If the repository is unreadable, no code owner is guessed and the verdict says tracing was unavailable. (SKILL.md:81)
25. five-category-classification: Each report gets exactly one of bug, performance (treated as a bug, with measurements kept), feature request, question or feedback, or reroute. (SKILL.md:85-105)
26. unclear-bug-vs-feature-no-file: When bug versus feature is unclear, nothing is filed, and the verdict may ask one focused question under the "other" marker. (SKILL.md:107)
27. evidence-based-route-matching: Routes match on confirmed product area, code path or error signature, never on the visible symptom alone when the trace points elsewhere. (SKILL.md:111-114)
28. unmatched-route-says-unclear: If no route matches, the verdict says the owner is unclear. (SKILL.md:115)
29. redirect-not-cross-post: The reporter is told in-thread where to take the issue, and the run never cross-posts. (SKILL.md:116)
30. four-condition-owner-ping-gate: A ping needs the map to name the owner, config to allow that ping type, a feature request needing owner input or strong evidence of a regression author, and an owner who is not a broad on-call group. (SKILL.md:118-125)
31. vendor-neutral-tracker-adapter-contract: The tracker adapter must search, read, create, update without clobbering, add source links and recurrence notes, and cancel, close or delete its own issue if the chat handoff fails. (SKILL.md:129-138)
32. per-write-fail-closed: A missing tracker operation fails closed for that write. (SKILL.md:140)
33. runtime-resolved-tracker-fields: Team, project, status and labels are resolved at runtime, and IDs, labels, owners and priority are never invented unless config requires them. (SKILL.md:142)
34. permalink-already-handled-check: If the permalink is already linked to an issue or a prior triage reply, nothing is posted or created. (SKILL.md:146)
35. dedupe-search-keys: Bug and performance reports are searched by signature, area, trigger, symptom, version or date window, suspected commit and permalink. (SKILL.md:148-156)
36. four-level-match-scale: Each search ends as a confident duplicate, possibly related, weak resemblance or no match, with the criteria for a confident duplicate defined. (SKILL.md:158-163)
37. confident-duplicate-recurrence-note: A confident duplicate gets the permalink and one short recurrence note, without reopening, relabelling or reassigning unless config says so. (SKILL.md:165)
38. possible-match-link-only: A possible match is linked as uncertain in the verdict, and nothing is created. (SKILL.md:167)
39. old-closed-issue-is-regression-lead: A long-closed issue is treated as a regression lead, not a live duplicate. (SKILL.md:169)
40. seven-condition-create-gate: An issue is created only for a clearly broken, still-live bug or performance report with no confident or plausible live match, a passing preflight, resolved tracker fields, and an adapter able to compensate. (SKILL.md:173-181)
41. never-create-list: Feature requests, questions, feedback, reroutes, possible or confident duplicates, and fixed issues are never filed. (SKILL.md:183)
42. self-contained-issue-template: A new issue has a plain area-and-symptom title, reporter quote, expected and observed behaviour, version or "unknown", trigger and frequency, permalink, labelled hypotheses, inline media where supported, artifact links, and the configured status and labels. (SKILL.md:185-196)
43. no-guessed-cause-in-title: The issue title never states a guessed root cause. (SKILL.md:198)
44. thread-ts-required-on-every-post: No source-channel post is ever made without a non-empty thread timestamp. (SKILL.md:202-204)
45. verdict-shape: The verdict leads with the outcome, links the issue, mentions a reroute or one missing fact if needed, has at most one allowed ping, and ends with exactly one marker line. (SKILL.md:206-212)
46. fixed-marker-contract: Markers take a fixed bracketed form for bug, performance or other, with an optional tracker URL, and the downstream repro trusts them only from the triage identity in this thread. (SKILL.md:214-224)
47. post-landing-verification-no-root-retry: After posting, the thread is reread to confirm the verdict landed, and failure is never retried at the root. (SKILL.md:226)
48. compensate-orphan-issue: If this run created an issue and the verdict did not land, the issue is cancelled, closed or deleted and that is verified, with any unverified compensation reported only in run output. (SKILL.md:228)
49. single-follow-up-window: For one follow-up window the run answers only direct questions, applies safe corrections to its issue, emits no second marker, avoids side chatter, stops early on request, extends at most once, and leaves new reports to new runs. (SKILL.md:232-240)
50. evidence-not-keyword-routing: A route needs evidence from the report or cause trace, and a keyword match alone is not enough. (references/routing.example.md:5)
51. route-schema: Each route has a name, match lists (product areas, code paths, error signatures), a destination (chat channel, tracker team), owners and a per-route feature-owner ping flag. (references/routing.example.md:7-37)
52. empty-fallback-destination: The fallback destination stays empty unless one team accepts all unmatched reports. (references/routing.example.md:39-42, 56)
53. ping-policy-allow-deny: Pings default off, are allowed for configured feature owners and confirmed regression authors, and are denied for broad on-call groups and unverified owners. (references/routing.example.md:44-51)
54. stable-match-keys: Routes use stable areas, paths and signatures. (references/routing.example.md:57)
55. no-private-data-in-public-copy: Published copies contain no private data and no raw user or channel IDs. (references/routing.example.md:58-59)
56. pings-off-until-team-agrees: Feature-owner pings stay off until the target team agrees. (references/routing.example.md:60)
57. reroute-without-cross-post: A reroute tells the reporter where to go, and the automation never cross-posts. (references/routing.example.md:61)

- `duplicate-search-key-list` (new): absent; reject; reason: A fixed key list adds a recipe (S-03): the adopted search asks for the same fault, not the same words, and which keys find it depends on the bead. Several keys (signature, version window, source link) also assume a chat report.
- `graded-duplicate-match` (new): absent; adopt, pending → triage; guide reword [U-04]; rewording: Mark an item a duplicate only when the match is confident; when it is only possibly related, link it in a note and keep deciding it on its own.; reason: Prevents: An item closed as a duplicate of one that only looks alike, which loses the report, or a related item left unlinked. Lands in triage, SKILL.md, Triage one bead, step 2. Upstream: SKILL.md:158-163; SKILL.md:165; SKILL.md:167.
- `closed-match-is-regression-lead` (new): absent; adopt, pending → triage; guide reword [U-04]; modification: Into `fixed-match-regression-lead`. Narrowed to a match closed as fixed, with evidence that the fixed behaviour has returned. Our tracker also closes items as wontfix, already built or duplicate; a match closed that way is no evidence of a regression and keeps the prior-rejection or duplicate check instead. Closure age alone decides nothing.; rewording: When the closest match is a bead closed as fixed and the report shows the fixed behaviour has returned, treat the item as a possible regression of it, not its duplicate; a match closed as wontfix or duplicate goes to the prior-rejection or duplicate check instead.; reason: Prevents: A fault that came back closed as a duplicate of the bead that once fixed it, so the regression goes unnoticed. Lands in triage, SKILL.md, Triage one bead, step 3, into `fixed-match-regression-lead`. Upstream: SKILL.md:169.
